LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD will only source the file and parse its top-level scope. The global scope consists entirely of standard variable assignments (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `optdepends`, `source`, `sha256sums`) and a `package()` function definition. None of these trigger any execution, network activity, or side effects during parsing. The `source` array simply defines a URL string with a variable expansion (`${pkgver}`), which is standard practice. The `package()` function body (which contains the binary invocation for completions) is defined but not called during `--printsrcinfo`. There is no top-level command substitution, no `eval`, no curl/wget, no obfuscated code, and no data exfiltration. The PKGBUILD is a clean, standard packaging file.</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard PKGBUILD with only variable assignments; safe to source.</summary>
</security_assessment>
